messages:
anya: Quick sprint recap — ran focused KV-cache quantization experiments (FP8 vs INT8) on llama-70b-kv variants. Key findings below, pls react with :eyes: for follow-up owners.

anya: TL;DR: FP8 KV -> ~42% mem reduction for KV buffers, median token latency ~same, but 95/99p cold-tail latency regressed on short prefix workloads (<=32 tokens). INT8 KV -> ~55% mem reduction, slightly higher median latency (+5-8ms) but better 99p than FP8 on some rigs.

anya: Raw bench snippets (inference single-node, sequence=512, batch=1, prefix=16/32):
```
Config        | KV format | KV mem GB | median ms/token | 95p ms/token | 99p ms/token
baseline fp16 | fp16      | 18.2      | 12.4            | 28.9         | 46.1
fp8-kv       | fp8       | 10.6      | 12.8            | 34.5         | 78.2
int8-kv      | int8      | 8.2       | 13.1            | 32.0         | 62.7
```

anya: Notable: FP8 gave big steady-state cost wins but occasional big 99p spikes during cold KV fills when prefix length small. Suspect dequant path and branch mispredicts in our kernel.

ci-bench-bot: automated-run: perf/1780543210/run-1 attached — full logs at https://ci/bench/1780543210 (contains per-layer timings, p50/p95/p99).

mike: Interesting — do we have per-layer KV size breakdown? my hunch: attention heads with large d_k are dominating.

rachel: Eval on eval-set-A (lm-head + R2 score vs reference):
- baseline fp16: Rouge-L 0.824, avg tok loss 1.92
- fp8-kv: Rouge-L 0.817 (-0.7 pts), loss 1.98 (+0.06)
- int8-kv: Rouge-L 0.821 (-0.3 pts), loss 1.94 (+0.02)
Small but measurable quality delta for FP8 in long-coherent contexts.

sophia: That matches what we saw: FP8 truncation noise in KV can cause divergence in repeated prefix sampling. Try stochastic rounding or per-channel scale recalc at K-V recompute? Could tradeoff perf.

tom: AWQ/GPTQ variants: we tried AWQ-kv on a micro-run — accuracy similar to INT8 but memory slightly higher. Also AWQ introduced more variability across seeds. Not promising for now.

mike: Can we try hybrid: FP8 for top X layers where KV matrix is largest (to save mem) and INT8 elsewhere to limit tail spikes? Also try increasing prefetch buffer to hide dequant cost.

anya: Good plan. I'll spin a small matrix: hybrid-(top4/top8/top12), stochastic rounding on fp8, int8 fallback threshold on 99p latency. Owners: @mike hybrid configs, @rachel quality evals, @sophia kernel tweaks, @tom AWQ followup.

deploy-bot: Canary run queued: canary/kvm-quant-hybrid-1780543210 starts in 2h, auto-rollback on 99p > 2x baseline.

mike: FYI, observed that CPU-side dequant cost dominates for short prefix. We should consider HW offload path or keep small-prefix path pinned to fp16.

rachel: Suggest adding a prompt-set focused eval (prefixes 2-20 tokens) since product has many micro-turn flows. I'll add that to the eval suite.

anya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after canary results + evals. Marking this thread as single-source of truth for the sprint notes. :white_check_mark:
